title: पूरी पुड़िया
logline: On her ninth wedding night a vanishing bride is caught doctoring the groom's milk. He is awake, he has padlocked the door, and he has spent fourteen months making himself her mark to reach the woman who sends the brides, and the bride who robbed his little brother. All he has of that bride is a photograph of her scarred left hand. The scar is on Kiran's arm, under her bangles.
language_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script, in the same line.
script_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script

characters.name: किरण (Kiran)
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride, on her ninth wedding night. Tonight she is 'स्नेहा' (Sneha) to the groom.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, closed watchful mouth. Low bun, centre parting with a thin line of sindoor, two loose strands at the temples, small round red bindi, thin plain gold ring in the LEFT nostril, small gold studs, short black-bead mangalsutra. Plain sindoor-red matte silk-cotton saree with a 1 cm plain gold border, red elbow-length blouse, pallu over the left shoulder; drawn over her head only in her first moments as 'Sneha'. Barefoot. Block henna: a solid disc in each palm and every fingertip dipped to the first joint, backs of the hands plain. On each forearm a red-and-ivory chooda that reads as one red cuff about 10 cm long with a pale band at each end. Tonight both cuffs are pushed up toward the elbows so they cannot clink. Her LEFT forearm is never seen uncovered until b11 (production lock).
characters.voice_note: Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge, small-city Madhya Pradesh Hindi. Two registers, one actor. 'Sneha' (l02, l06): half a tone higher, soft, shy, आप, sentences that trail off. Kiran (from l11): lower, flat, quick, तुम, short sentences. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill.

characters.name: आदित्य (Aditya)
characters.role: The groom. A pharmacist who has made himself the bureau's mark to find the woman who sends the brides, and the bride who robbed his brother Mohit.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow with a slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, high forehead, calm deep-set eyes, thin mouth, short neat black hair with a left side parting. Rimless rectangular glasses in every shot, including with his eyes shut. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta with a band collar and three cloth buttons, sleeves folded back once, a side pocket on the right; cream churidar; barefoot. A brass key about 5 cm long on a doubled red cotton thread, outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch on a brown strap on the left wrist, never readable.
characters.voice_note: Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Educated small-city Madhya Pradesh Hindi in full sentences, तुम to Kiran, English nouns of his trade (sedative, SIM, proof, police, bureau, photo, reception). Even and unhurried, almost courteous, like a man reading out a prescription. Never shouts. Under pressure he slows down and drops in volume; the one place the voice may catch is his brother's name.

characters.name: बिल्लू (Billu)
characters.role: The bride's 'brother', driver and lookout. Waiting in the car in the lane.
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry and restless. Brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, black hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket with the sleeves pushed up over a black round-neck T-shirt, dark jeans. A wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth; a car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal, talks round a toothpick. Small-town Bundelkhand street Hindi, Hindi-heavy. To Mausi: quick and obedient.

characters.name: शकुन मौसी (Shakun Mausi)
characters.role: Runs the bureau and the brides. Voice on Billu's phone only; never seen in this episode.
characters.look: Not seen in s1e01. Voice only.
characters.voice_note: Female, mid 50s, low, warm and grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Bundelkhand-side Hindi, Hindi-heavy, trade English only (phone). An endearment in every second line. Laughs easily; never raises her voice. On the phone she is fully voiced and clear, never a whisper. Light phone filter in the mix.

characters.name: मोहित (Mohit)
characters.role: Aditya's dead younger brother. Only a hand in the photograph; no voice. His death is never pictured.
characters.look: Only in the photograph (b9): a young man's right hand, palm up, light-brown skin, a red thread at the wrist, the cuff of a cream kurta. Never a face.

location: The bridal bedroom of a rented house (first floor, about 3 by 3.5 m): double bed with a dark wood headboard against the back wall, white sheet, one red bolster, loose marigold petals, marigold strings in a fringe above the headboard; lime-washed pale-green walls, one bare nail, no pictures. From the foot of the bed facing it: the window with an iron grille and open shutters in the RIGHT wall, the grey-green steel almirah against the LEFT wall with a wooden chair holding Kiran's maroon bag, the pale-blue double door BEHIND, bolted and padlocked on the inside. A low stool on the window side of the bed holds a steel tray with the steel glass and the paper fold. One warm amber bedside lamp on the almirah side (key), cool blue-white streetlight through the grille (rim), no overhead light. Cutaway: the empty lane below, Billu's old white sedan under one sodium streetlight, shutters down, no readable signs.
time_of_day: Night 1, late April, about 1:35 to 1:45 am. Warm night, window open.

beats.action: HOOK, the image lands at 0 s. Set-up 1 (from the start of l01): extreme close-up of Kiran's RIGHT hand, fingertips dipped in henna, tapping white powder from a small folded paper पुड़िया into a steel glass of pale-yellow kesar milk on the steel tray on the stool by the window. Her right chooda is pushed up toward the elbow, out of frame or at its edge; the red pallu at frame edge. Her left arm is not in frame: it is under the fall of the pallu (production lock, b1 to b10). Warm lamp key, cool streetlight rim. l01 is Aditya off screen, lying dressed on the bed with his eyes shut. Set-up 2 (from 'आधी में'): the same framing, the hand stopped in the air, half the powder still in the fold.

sfx_notes: Bedroom bed, b1 to b4 and b6 to b11, loopable: a warm April night through the open window, crickets, one far dog, a truck on a distant highway. Close, dry room tone. No ceiling fan anywhere in the episode (Mohit).
b1: paper tapped on the steel rim, a faint hiss of powder into milk. Aditya's l01 is off screen but close and dry, not distant: he is two metres away. Every sound stops with her hand on 'आधी में'.
b2: the bed creaks and marigold petals rustle as he sits up.
b3: bare feet on the floor; the iron bolt rattles against the hasp; the brass padlock knocks once on the iron and holds.
b4: the steel almirah door creaks; the velvet box hinge. The phone makes no sound.

b5: lane exterior: sodium-lamp hum, crickets, the toothpick clicking on Billu's teeth. Mausi through a light phone filter, fully voiced and warm, wide enough that consonants survive. Duck the lane bed under l27 so the names 'स्नेहा' and 'किरण' are both clear (the duck moves from l10 to l27 in the clarity pass).
b6 to b8: room tone only. Nothing under l13.
b8, l23: paper drawn from cloth; the print's crease.
b9, l29: room tone only under the photograph insert, so the line is fully clear.
b10: the crickets drop out under l25 and stay out through Kiran's hold.
b11: bed and music duck right down under l26 so it is fully clear. Last sound: one faint dry click of the chooda's bangles as the cuff slides down, close and small, then black and silence.
music_note: No music for b1 to b4: breath, paper and the padlock. A single low drone enters on the lane cut (b5) at the edge of hearing and carries under b6 and b8, never above the dialogue. It drops out entirely under l25. A low sustained note swells on the scar insert in b11 and cuts dead with the picture, leaving the bangle click alone.
ending_question: जिस हाथ के लिए आदित्य चौदह महीने भटका, वो उसी कमरे में चूड़े के नीचे है: वो कलाई कब देखेगा, और देखकर क्या करेगा?

clarity_pass.scope: Dialogue only (Option 1). Every beat id, its order, staging and shot mapping is kept; no shot is added or changed. Story, ending question and locked lines are unchanged.
clarity_pass.metadata_only: l01 gains heard_as off_screen; l09 and l10 gain heard_as phone. Their text is byte-identical for l01 and changed for l09 and l10 (reworded above).

fixes.fault: Orchestrator read item 1: 'Nobody has told us this is a wedding night, she is the bride.' Ledger s1e01.f01: the time super gives both roles by the end of b2.

cv_A s1e01 (2) and cv_B: 'The set is brass. The house is rented by the month.' had to be worked out. Adds 'यहाँ चुराने को कुछ नहीं।' so the premise (a bride who came to rob) is spoken by the end of b4, the first-third marker.
Orchestrator item 6: new place, new people, nobody placed. Billu now says where he is ('नीचे गाड़ी में हूँ'), which ties the car below to 'गाड़ी में भैया' in l13 (cv_A s1e01 (3)).

cv_A s1e01 (3): 'Billu is never named here.' Mausi names him; the name_role super sits on set-up 2 because set-up 1 carries the 1:40 overlay. 'बेटा' is replaced so the first 'beta' a viewer hears on the s1e02 call is for Kiran (ledger name_clashes).
Orchestrator item 7: 'I'll phone her at two' had no clear 'her'. 'दुल्हन को' points at the bride behind the lit window.

cv_A s1e01 (1), cv_B 'Who is who', review cause 5: nothing links Sneha to Kiran. l27 bridges the alias once, out of Aditya's hearing (lock). The name moves out of l10, which keeps Mausi's fretting (balance lever) as 'बच्ची सुबह से भूखी होगी'.
Orchestrator item 9: 'Jumps from pleading to cold with no turn.' 'नाटक ख़त्म' says aloud that the shy bride was an act, matching the pallu pushed back in set-up 1.

cv_A s1e01 (6) and D-024 evidence: Aditya is never named on path A. l28 names him, says the bureau holds a fake name (sets up s1b01 'Your name is fake') and glosses 'bureau' as 'marriage bureau' before the protected l13 (cv_A s1e01 (3) 'Bureau is never explained').
cv_A s1e01 (4), cv_B: 'party' means nothing to a new viewer. Glossed in the same line ('यानी लुटने वाला दूल्हा'), because the word recurs on both paths (ledger glossary).
cv_B s1e01: 'Take it all. Open the padlock.' Take what? The money is with Mausi. Now 'सब तुम्हें दिलवा दूँगी', which she can offer.

cv_B s1e01: 'He wants two different people within one minute... Which one is his goal?' The because comes back: the police told him to bring proof (l17), so for the proof he wants the woman who sends the brides (l18). The hand (l26) is then his own aim. l17 also plants s1a02's 'the police in my town'.

Orchestrator item 13 and cv_B: Mohit's story was fragments ('There was no reception', 'The bureau sent no photo. The bride took his phone.'). Now: the bride vanished with everything; the bureau never sent her photo; she took Mohit's phone; this one print survived, which Mohit sent from the temple. 'उसने' in l24 became 'मोहित ने' so the sender is not read as the bride.

cv_A s1e01 (5), cv_B, review cause 4: the photograph's burn is the clue the whole series rests on and no line said it. l29 says what the picture shows and not whose it is. It plays over the photograph insert (s31) so the viewer hears it while seeing it; see writer_notes for why this differs from the ledger's placement on set-up 1.
